references.text: The command to eat unleavened bread together with the Passover lamb for seven days originates from the original Passover ordinance in Egypt.
The instruction to eat unleavened bread for seven days and remove all yeast from the houses during the Feast of Unleavened Bread.
The explanation for why the Israelites ate unleavened bread: they were driven out of Egypt in haste and had no time to let the dough rise.
Moses commands the people to remember the day they left Egypt, and that nothing leavened shall be eaten.
Unleavened bread shall be eaten for seven days, and no yeast shall be found with you.
The command to observe the Feast of Unleavened Bread and eat unleavened bread for seven days as a memorial of the exodus from Egypt.
Reiteration of the command regarding the Feast of Unleavened Bread in the month of Abib, when Israel went out of Egypt.
The institution of the Feast of Unleavened Bread on the fifteenth day of the first month, with unleavened bread for seven days.
The feast on the fifteenth day of the first month where unleavened bread is to be eaten for seven days.
Paul applies the image of unleavened bread as a symbol of purity and truth in Christian celebration.
